title: Chapter 76 — Reading People: Signals, Styles, and Tension
intro: Decision styles, body language, listening below the words, and adapting your approach to the person in front of you.

sections.title: Not Every Customer Shops the Same Way
sections.content:
Some customers want details. Give them specs, comparisons, and data. Some customers want speed. Get to the point and do not waste their time. Some customers want reassurance. Walk them through the decision slowly and patiently. Some customers want to be in control. Let them lead and support their process.

Recognizing which style you are dealing with — and adapting your approach — is one of the most valuable skills on the floor. It is the difference between connecting and colliding.

sections.title: Body Language Tells the Truth
sections.content:
When a customer says 'I like it' but their arms are crossed and they are leaning back — they do not like it. When a customer says 'the price is fine' but they wince — the price is not fine.

Watch for alignment between words and body language. When they match, the customer is being honest. When they do not match, the body is usually telling the truth.

This is not mind reading. It is paying attention. And it only works if you are looking at the customer instead of looking at your phone or the product.

sections.title: Listening Below the Words
sections.content:
What a customer says and what they mean are often different. 'We are just looking' often means 'we are not ready to be sold to yet.' 'It is too expensive' often means 'I do not see the value.' 'I need to think about it' often means 'something is bothering me but I do not want to say it.'

The 10 Steps — especially Discovery — are designed to get below the surface. The deeper you listen, the better you serve.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating reading people, ask:

Does the salesperson adapt their approach to different customer styles — or use the same method every time?
Do they notice body language signals that contradict spoken words?
Do they listen for meaning below the surface — or take everything at face value?
Do they adjust when they sense tension — or push through it?
